editorialLexicalPolicy.evidenceBoundary: Spanish realization options and constraints only. These entries never override source surface, morphology, syntax, discourse, or canonical corpus evidence.
editorialLexicalPolicy.instruction: Express physical or figurative turning/returning without adding sorrow or a change of mind unless separate evidence states it.

spanishOptions.when: Return to a person, place, state, or prior course is in view.
A natural spatial or figurative return is in view.
Direction or orientation changes toward or away from an expressed object.
A real religious reorientation is in view and the Spanish does not falsely suggest exchanging one religion for another.

avoid: adding a mental change not otherwise expressed

editorialLexicalPolicy.evidenceBoundary: Spanish realization options and constraints only. These entries never override source surface, morphology, syntax, discourse, or canonical corpus evidence.
editorialLexicalPolicy.instruction: Preserve the bodily act and determine its relational force from the recipient and context. Adorar is permitted when genuine divine or idolatrous worship is expressed, but it is never an automatic gloss and must not make a human recipient divine.

spanishOptions.when: A divine or idolatrous recipient and the construction genuinely express religious worship.
The bodily gesture is foregrounded, including respect, submission, entreaty, or worship.
The act is directed to an authority or honored person without presenting that recipient as divine.

avoid: using adorar as an automatic gloss
inferring solely from the verb that the recipient is divine
reducing genuine worship to a merely physical gesture when the context establishes worship

editorialLexicalPolicy.evidenceBoundary: Spanish realization options and constraints only. These entries never override source surface, morphology, syntax, discourse, or canonical corpus evidence.
editorialLexicalPolicy.instruction: Preserve the source relation of work or service. When the service is cultual, express that cultual relation without erasing the service component or merging it with a separate bowing token.

spanishOptions.when: Service to a person, authority, people, deity, or idol is foregrounded.
The construction explicitly presents cultual service and natural Spanish benefits from making that relation explicit.

avoid: using adorar as an automatic replacement
merging service with a separate bowing or homage token

editorialLexicalPolicyReview.title: Arrepentimiento, pesar y cambio de rumbo
editorialLexicalPolicyReview.summary: The source verb marks turning or returning; other concepts require their own source support.

editorialLexicalPolicyReview.title: Adorar, postrarse, servir y rendir culto
editorialLexicalPolicyReview.summary: Canonical and contemporary usage applies bowing and prostration to God, idols, rulers, relatives, and honored persons; recipient and context determine the Spanish relation.

editorialLexicalPolicyReview.title: Adorar, postrarse, servir y rendir culto
editorialLexicalPolicyReview.summary: Abad spans ordinary work, political or personal service, and service to God or idols; its service relation must remain visible.
